title: Joint Probability Matrix Model Valuation
text: To ground the semantics of joint random variables, consider two binary variables X and Y evaluated over a discrete grid. Variable X represents server availability taking values in {0, 1}, and Y represents network congestion taking values in {0, 1}. We construct a 2-by-2 joint probability distribution model assigning concrete truth values to each state: P(X=0, Y=0) = 0.05, P(X=0, Y=1) = 0.15, P(X=1, Y=0) = 0.60, and P(X=1, Y=1) = 0.20. By summing across columns, we compute the marginal distribution of X: P(X=1) = 0.80, representing an 80% overall server uptime. By summing across rows, we compute P(Y=1) = 0.35. We evaluate the conditional probability P(Y=1 | X=1) as 0.20 divided by 0.80, which equals 0.25. This concrete state-space model provides an explicit valuation across all possible systemic configurations, illustrating the interaction between marginal probabilities and conditional dependencies.
